data.title: Spooky end of the month for stocks? SA analyst sees a bull run into year-end
data.description:
Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research believes the stock market will see a much desired runup by the end of the year.

“We are calling for a bull run in equities into year-end,” King said.

Despite the ongoing equity selloff, led by semiconductors and the overall artificial intelligence-adjacent sector, King said market conditions are ripe for a rally.

U.S. Treasury yields , , , and the U.S. dollar are on the wane, while high-beta assets, such as cryptocurrencies, “are proving resilient in times of stress.”

The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.93%, while the 2-year Treasury yield is 4.59%. The 30-year Treasury yield is 5.31%.

Bitcoin has declined 7.6% in the past month, and it is trading at around $76,850.

The S&P 500 (SP500) finished -1.8%, while the Nasdaq Composite closed -2.9%, and the Dow ended -1.1%.

“Even today’s 3% drop in the Nasdaq held up and is over the critical 200-day moving average,” he added. “Ignore sentiment; focus on price."

data.title: State Department approves $2.1B Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
data.description:
The U.S. State Department said Friday it approved the sale of as many as 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles, as well as spare parts, logistics, and support, to Ukraine for $2.1B.

Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor for the ‌sale; in July, the U.S. Army awarded the company a contract ​worth up to $58.6B to produce ⁠Patriot interceptor missiles.

The PAC-3 is the most advanced Patriot missile; it uses "hit-to-kill" kinetic energy - colliding directly with targets at over Mach 5 - rather than a blast fragmentation warhead, featuring a dual-pulse solid rocket motor and larger fins for extended range and maneuverability against ballistic and hypersonic threats, according to the Lockheed Martin website.

Ukraine will pay for the Patriot order with "donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds, financed by the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan," and no U.S. funds are involved in the sale, the State Department said.

Ukraine's President ​Zelenskyy said earlier this week that his country had been waiting for nearly a month ​for the U.S. to sign off on critical missile supplies, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.

data.title: Nasdaq tanks 5% in October as tech bloodbath deepens
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index plummeted nearly 3% on Friday amid a wider selloff in the technology sector, intensified by Intel’s weak third-quarter results.

The tech-heavy index closed 2.86% lower at 25,437 points, recording its worst single-day performance since June.

Intel’s shares nosedived during Friday’s trading session, closing 29.38% lower after its Q3 results showed guidance that missed Wall Street estimates by a considerable margin. Its peers Sandisk and Qualcomm also took a hit, ending 13.42% and 11.12% lower, respectively.

For the week, Nasdaq slumped 2.79%, while for the month, it tanked 5.30%.

The index closed lower in 11 of October’s 21 trading sessions, capping a volatile month that began with the Nasdaq notching record highs. Investor sentiment swung between concerns over rising AI capital expenditure and optimism following the Federal Reserve’s dovish stance on interest rates. Meanwhile, intermittent selling across the tech sector intensified towards month-end following disappointing results from Big Tech companies like Alphabet (GGOG) and Amazon .

data.title: The Week the Cracks in the AI Trade Grew Deeper — WSJ
data.description:
By David Uberti and Hannah Erin Lang

Slowing growth. Dwindling cash piles. Cannibalized business lines. Pressure points are multiplying across the artificial-intelligence boom that has propelled markets and the economy.

The cracks in the AI trade multiplied through the week, culminating in a sharp tech selloff Friday that sent the Nasdaq composite to its worst day since June and its worst month in more than a year.

The vulnerabilities in Wall Street's favorite trade have been building for months, periodically appearing around smaller companies drowning in debt. Each time, the largest firms behind America's AI build-out have reassured Wall Street by printing profits, suggesting the show will go on even in a world of higher interest rates.

This week was different. After tech stocks had treaded water for weeks, AI giant Anthropic momentarily rejuvenated investors with a filing that showed soaring revenue ahead of its planned initial public offering. But then publicly traded tech firms reported earnings — and markets got a reality check.

First came a dissatisfying quarterly report from Alphabet, which showed that growth in Google's search-advertising business slowed — in part because of the impact of "AI mode" queries. Traders punished the stock with a 13% decline Thursday that marked its worst day on record, hammering major Alphabet shareholders such as Berkshire Hathaway.

Then the bad tech vibes got worse. Late Thursday, Amazon reported plunging free cash flow and revenue that missed analyst estimates. American chipmaking giant Intel forecast a prolonged slowdown in personal-computer sales, pressured by memory chip prices sent skyrocketing by the AI boom.

Intel shares on Friday crashed about 30%, the worst session on record for a company that has traded on the U.S. stock market for decades. The plunge vaporized more than $15 billion in combined paper holdings by two of the company's largest shareholders: the U.S. government and Nvidia.

Write to David Uberti at david.uberti@wsj.com and Hannah Erin Lang at hannaherin.lang@wsj.com

data.title: In a wild October for markets, these stocks were the biggest winners and losers
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

Many Big Tech stocks were hit hard but the S&P 500 showed strength under the surface, with a majority of stocks showing gains for the month

Intel was the worst-performing stock in the S&P 500 during October with a 43.5% decline, while Alphabet was down 18.5%.

October has seen a lot of carnage in tech stocks, but you might not guess that from the S&P 500's performance.

The S&P 500 SPX was down 0.5% for October through Friday morning, even though 75% of stocks in the large-cap benchmark index were up for the month.

The S&P 500 is about 40% concentrated in its largest 10 stocks by market capitalization. Meanwhile, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP was up 5.5% for October - reflecting the underlying strength in stocks, even as many of the largest technology companies have fared poorly as investors question the AI infrastructure build-out. And as you can see below on the list of the month's worst performers, even non-IT companies, such as Caterpillar (CAT), were hit hard during what might be a temporary backlash against the rapid pace of data-center construction.

Among the largest 10 components of the S&P 500, Nvidia (NVDA) (the largest of all) was down 8.7% for October, while Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) was down 18.5%, Amazon.com (AMZN) was down 6.9%, Broadcom (AVGO) was down 5.6%, Meta Platforms (META) was down 14.7% and Micron Technology (MU) was down 16.8%. data.title: Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,000
data.description:
The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000, government data showed on Friday, as authorities had yet to find a way to control the country's deadliest Ebola epidemic on record.

There are no approved treatments or vaccines to combat the rare Bundibugyo species, which is behind the outbreak in the Central African country.

It has infected more than 10,000 people since it was declared in May.

Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have helped the virus spread more rapidly than in previous outbreaks.

Eight of Congo's 26 provinces have been affected, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centres.

This year's outbreak is the world's second-largest ever, behind only the 2014-2016 one that infected over 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000 across ​Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

Last week Nigeria became the fourth African country to report an Ebola case, extending the outbreak's geographic spread to West Africa. East African countries Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases.

data.title: CME cattle futures close lower as cash market cools; lean hogs lower
data.description:
By P.J. Huffstutter

Cattle futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) closed sharply lower on Friday, with the most-active December live cattle contract sliding for the fourth straight session, as cash market prices softened and fund investors looked to liquidate their positions, market analysts said.

Trades in the cash cattle markets have been somewhat sluggish, and prices have also cooled, market analysts said. Dressed purchases in Nebraska were down at least $4 per cwt from last week and down $2 to $5 per cwt in other Midwestern markets.

CME December live cattle settled down 5.350 cents at 220.950 cents per pound — the contract's lowest price since October 6. Meanwhile, February ended down 5.275 cents at 224.200 cents per pound.

Meanwhile, CME feeder cattle contracts have been seeing more volatility recently, as more investors are trading in the cattle market, analysts said. CME January feeders finished the day down 10.175 cents at 331.775 cents per pound.

CME lean hog futures also turned lower, with both the February and April 2027 contracts setting fresh lows, on seasonal pressure, plentiful hog supplies, weak cash prices and slumping wholesale pork prices.

"This is a cash-led bear market," said Don Roose, president of Iowa-based U.S. Commodities.

CME December lean hog futures (LHZ26) settled down 0.95 cent at 58.875 cents per pound, and notched a weekly loss for the fourth consecutive week. February hog futures (LHG27) ended 0.975 cent lower at 63.75 cents per pound on Friday.

The CME's Lean Hog Index (.IHX), a two-day weighted average of cash hog prices, was last quoted at 67.30 cents per pound, its lowest value since January 2024. The US Department of Agriculture priced pork carcasses on Friday afternoon at $70.10 per hundredweight, down 59 cents from Thursday, though bellies firmed $7.19 at $72.85 per cwt.

data.title: Aspen Neuroscience, Autologous Cell Therapies for Neurological Disease, Files for Nasdaq IPO
data.description:
Aspen Neuroscience, Inc. is offering 9,375,000 shares of common stock in its initial public offering at $15.00 per share, for gross proceeds of approximately $140.6 million. The company’s shares are approved to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ASPE. Aspen plans to use the proceeds primarily to advance its Parkinson’s disease cell therapy candidate through clinical development, including a planned Phase 3 trial.

Business Description

Aspen Neuroscience develops therapies made from a patient’s own induced-pluripotent stem cells, which are reprogrammed from adult cells and then differentiated into specialized cells. Its lead candidate, sasineprocel, is a one-time cell therapy being studied for Parkinson’s disease. The treatment is designed to replace lost dopamine-producing neurons and is delivered to the brain through stereotactic surgery. In an ongoing open-label Phase 1/2a trial, 15 patients had been treated as of August 18, 2026; the company reported preliminary safety observations and improvements across several measures, while noting that the study has no control group and the results are not yet conclusive.

Aspen’s platform also supports a preclinical program developing gene-corrected microglia cells for pediatric leukodystrophies. The company manufactures its clinical candidate in San Diego and is developing automated processes using third-party platforms, with the goal of supporting production for later-stage trials and potential commercialization. Its approach is intended to avoid the long-term immunosuppression often required for donor-derived cell therapies, but the company faces clinical, regulatory, manufacturing, financing, and commercialization risks.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: The prospectus estimates that about 300,000 U.S. patients with Parkinson’s disease are refractory to dopamine replacement therapy, with approximately half potentially eligible for cell replacement surgery; it does not provide a market-value estimate.
  • Market growth: Parkinson’s disease prevalence has doubled globally over the past 25 years; the prospectus projects 25.2 million people worldwide will be living with the disease by 2050, a 112% increase from 2021.
  • Market position: Aspen is a clinical-stage developer of autologous induced-pluripotent stem cell therapies, with sasineprocel in Phase 1/2a testing for Parkinson’s disease.
  • Key competitors: Parkinson’s disease competitors include BlueRock Therapeutics/Bayer, Sumitomo, Hope Bio, Oryon, Kenai Therapeutics, and gene therapy developers such as AskBio/Bayer and MeiraGTx.
  • Industry trends: Cell replacement approaches seek to restore dopamine-producing neurons; autologous therapies may avoid long-term immunosuppression, while automated manufacturing aims to improve consistency and scale.

Operational Metrics

  • Clinical trial: 15 patients had received sasineprocel in the Phase 1/2a ASPIRO trial as of August 18, 2026; seven received a low dose and eight a high dose.
  • Clinical follow-up: All 12 patients in the first three trial cohorts had at least one follow-up evaluation six months or later as of the data cutoff.
  • Manufacturing capacity: The company is designing a modular automated process intended to support production for hundreds of patients annually per module.
  • Manufacturing timelines: The three production stages take approximately three weeks, eight weeks, and five weeks, respectively, with quality-control testing typically requiring an additional four to five weeks.
  • Employees: Aspen had 120 full-time employees and three part-time employees as of June 30, 2026.
  • Geographic presence: The company is headquartered and operates its clinical manufacturing facility in San Diego, California; its initial commercial focus is North America.
  • Partnerships and licenses: Key third parties include Cell X Technologies, Mytos Bio, ClearPoint Neuro, iPS Academia Japan, Sumitomo Pharma/RACTHERA, The Cleveland Clinic Foundation, and the Scripps Research Institute.
  • Pipeline: Sasineprocel is in Phase 1/2a development for Parkinson’s disease; the microglia program remains preclinical, with IND-enabling studies expected to begin in the second half of 2027.

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): No product revenue to date; the company reported no revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
  • Revenue growth: Not applicable; Aspen has not generated product revenue.
  • Operating income: Operating loss of $38.2 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
  • Net income: Net loss of $36.5 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026.

Management

  • Damien McDevitt, President, Chief Executive Officer and Director - Previously led Akcea Therapeutics as CEO and held leadership roles at Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Acadia Pharmaceuticals, and GlaxoSmithKline.
  • Faheem Hasnain, Executive Chairman - Co-founder, chairman, and CEO of Gossamer Bio; previously led Receptos before its acquisition by Celgene and held senior roles at other biotechnology companies.
  • Dalen Meeter, Chief Financial Officer - Previously served as CFO of Singular Genomics and held finance leadership roles at Illumina; began his career at KPMG.
  • Lisa Johnson-Pratt, Sasineprocel Development Lead and Chief Commercial Officer - Has held leadership roles in clinical development, medical affairs, and commercialization at Aspen, Ionis, Akcea, GSK, and Merck.
  • Kim Raineri, Chief Technology Officer - Previously held manufacturing and operations leadership roles at Tectonic Therapeutic, Nikon CeLL innovation, Lonza, and CryoLife.

IPO Structure

  • Filing date: October 30, 2026

  • Shares offered: 9,375,000 shares, plus an underwriters’ option to purchase up to 1,406,250 additional shares
  • Lead underwriters: Leerink Partners, Piper Sandler, Stifel, UBS Investment Bank, and Oppenheimer & Co.
  • Use of proceeds: Approximately $8.0 million for the Phase 1/2a ASPIRO trial, $110.0 million for a planned Phase 3 trial, $4.0 million for microglia programs, and the remainder for working capital and general corporate purposes.

data.title: Accendra Health Receives Continued Listing Standard Notice from NYSE Regarding Market Capitalization and Stockholders’ Equity; Intends to Submit Business Plan and Return to Compliance with NYSE Listing Standard​
data.description:
Accendra Health, Inc. () (the Company) today announced that on October 27, 2026, it received a notice (the “Notice”) from the New York Stock Exchange (the “NYSE”) notifying the Company that it is not in compliance with Section 802.01B of the NYSE’s continued listing standards that the Company have an average market capitalization of not less than $50.0 million over a consecutive 30 trading-day period and stockholders’ equity of not less than $50.0 million. The Notice does not result in the immediate delisting of the Company’s Class A Common Stock (the “Common Stock”) from the NYSE.

The Company intends to respond to the NYSE within ten business days of receipt of the Notice affirming its intent to submit a business plan. Pursuant to Section 802.01B, the Company has a period of 45 calendar days following receipt of the Notice to submit a business plan that demonstrates how the Company intends to regain compliance with Section 802.01B within 18 months of receipt of the Notice. The NYSE will review the business plan and, if accepted, the Company will be subject to quarterly monitoring by the NYSE of the progress of the business plan.

​​The Company’s Common Stock will continue to be listed and trade on the NYSE during this period, subject to its compliance with other NYSE continued listing standards. The receipt of the Notice does not affect the Company’s business, operations or reporting requirements with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Risk Factors,” as applicable, and subsequent quarterly reports on Form 10-Q and current reports on Form 8-K filed with or furnished to the SEC, for a discussion of certain known risk factors that could cause the Company’s actual results to differ materially from its current estimates. These filings are available at www.accendrahealth.com. Given these risks and uncertainties, the Company can give no assurance that any forward-looking statements will, in fact, transpire and, therefore, cautions investors not to place undue reliance on them. About Accendra Health

Accendra Health, Inc. () is a leading nationwide provider of products, technology, and services that support health beyond the hospital for millions of people each year.
